title: Rafael and the Orbit
premise: Mirabel Villalobos smuggles memories through orbital customs while tending a beacon whose original commission records have been erased, making her the last person who knows why it exists. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew aged backward and their memories of a colonial massacre intact but unverifiable, customs authorities move to purge both ship and witness. Mirabel must trace the beacon's hidden origin to prove the massacre happened, discovering it was built as a memorial by the massacre's only escaped survivor—her own grandmother. In the end she broadcasts the truth through the beacon at the cost of her smuggling network and her freedom, choosing memory over survival.
about_author: Elodie Okonkwo is a former radio astronomer who left research to write fiction about the stories institutions choose to forget. She lives between Lagos and Lisbon, where she collects obsolete recording formats.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Mirabel runs contraband memories past customs while maintaining an unregistered beacon on the station's edge. POV: Mirabel. Establishes her invisibility as survival strategy; ends with her noticing the beacon pulsed without input.

chapters.title: Customs and Consequences
chapters.summary: A near-miss inspection forces Mirabel to dump a client's dying-mother memory into the void. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: guilt over what she destroys to stay safe.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: The Halcyon docks, crew aged backward twenty years, claiming they never left. POV: Customs officer Adeyemi, skeptical and uneasy. Beat: wrongness that can't be filed away.

chapters.title: A Memory That Isn't Mine
chapters.summary: A young crewman, Tomas, secretly gives Mirabel a memory chip: footage of the Kestrel Colony burning. POV: alternating Mirabel/Tomas. Beat: horror and the first crack in her neutrality.

chapters.title: Records Say Otherwise
chapters.summary: Official archives show Kestrel Colony was never settled. Adeyemi is ordered to impound the Halcyon and detain its crew. POV: Adeyemi. Beat: duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: The Purge Order
chapters.summary: Authorities schedule a full memory-wipe of the Halcyon crew. Tomas begs Mirabel to hide him. POV: Mirabel. Beat: invisibility is no longer possible; she must choose.

chapters.title: Hiding in Plain Orbit
chapters.summary: Mirabel stows Tomas among her smuggling routes, using client memories as decoys. POV: Mirabel. Beat: tenderness growing between them amid fear.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel realizes the beacon's pulse pattern matches the Halcyon's distress frequency—it's been calling the ship home for decades. POV: Mirabel. Beat: revelation that her quiet duty has purpose.

chapters.title: The Commission File
chapters.summary: Digging into erased records, Mirabel finds a redacted name: E. Villalobos. Her grandmother commissioned the beacon. POV: Mirabel. Beat: personal history colliding with public erasure.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Hands
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Elena Villalobos escapes Kestrel Colony as it burns, carrying a data core of the massacre. POV: Elena (interpolated). Beat: inherited trauma, the origin of everything.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Doubt
chapters.summary: Adeyemi finds falsified logs in his own department and realizes the purge order predates the Halcyon's return. POV: Adeyemi. Beat: the hunter suspecting the hunt.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Mirabel's network is compromised protecting Tomas; her fence is arrested. POV: Mirabel. Beat: the cost of belonging to something again.

chapters.title: Tomas, Aged Eleven
chapters.summary: The reversal accelerates; Tomas begins losing adult memories, including pieces of the massacre evidence—and of Mirabel. POV: Tomas. Beat: love against a clock.

chapters.title: The Core
chapters.summary: Elena's data core is inside the beacon itself; the 'maintenance' Mirabel performed was unknowing preservation. POV: Mirabel. Beat: awe—she was chosen before she was born.

chapters.title: They Know
chapters.summary: Security traces Tomas to Mirabel; a raid forces them to flee to the beacon array. POV: alternating. Beat: pursuit, adrenaline, no way back.

chapters.title: Adeyemi Turns
chapters.summary: Adeyemi confronts Mirabel at the array—but instead of arresting her, he brings the falsification evidence he's collected. POV: Adeyemi. Beat: duty realigned with conscience.

chapters.title: Broadcast Window
chapters.summary: The beacon can transmit the core once per orbit cycle; the next window coincides with the purge team's arrival. POV: Mirabel. Beat: ticking clock, plan forming.

chapters.title: The Wipe Begins
chapters.summary: Purge teams board the Halcyon; Tomas, now childlike, hides in the array while Mirabel fights to reach the transmitter. POV: alternating. Beat: desperation, sacrifice looming.

chapters.title: Kestrel, Burning
chapters.summary: Climax: Mirabel triggers the broadcast—the massacre plays across every public screen in the system, unerasable, witnessed by thousands. POV: Mirabel. Beat: triumph shadowed by sirens closing in.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: The system erupts; inquiries open; the Halcyon crew's memories are preserved instead of wiped. But Mirabel is taken into custody. POV: Adeyemi. Beat: justice arriving too late to be clean.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Months later: Mirabel, released under amnesty, visits Tomas—who remembers nothing of her but feels he should. POV: Mirabel. Beat: grief and grace; love outliving memory.

chapters.title: The Beacon Still Sings
chapters.summary: Mirabel formally registers the beacon as a memorial, its commission restored under Elena Villalobos's name. She stays—not invisible anymore, but seen. POV: Mirabel. Beat: belonging earned at a price; quiet, hard-won peace.
